questions.prompt: `Person` is declared as `public record Person(string FirstName, string LastName);`. What does this print?
questions.explanation: `with` creates a copy of the record with the listed changes, and records get an auto-generated `ToString()` in the form `Person { FirstName = Aman, LastName = Singh }`. `p1` is unchanged.

questions.prompt: `Person` is the same positional record. What does this print?
options: It does not compile, because records can't be compared
questions.explanation: Records use value-based equality, so two records with the same values are equal. For normal classes, which use reference equality by default, the result would be `False`.

questions.prompt: With `public record Person(string FirstName, string LastName);`, what happens with `p.FirstName = "John";` after the object is created?
options: It changes the name, because record properties are ordinary setters
It creates a new record automatically
It is an error, because positional records create init-only properties
It compiles, but the change is ignored
questions.explanation: A positional record creates init-only properties, so they can't be assigned after creation. Use a `with` expression to get a modified copy, or declare the properties with `set` for a mutable record.

questions.prompt: Put the steps a hash-based collection such as `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` follows to find a key in order.
steps: Call `GetHashCode()` on the key to select a bucket
Search only inside that bucket instead of checking every item
Call `Equals()` to confirm the exact matching object
questions.explanation: The hash code narrows the search to one bucket, and `Equals()` confirms the match. That is why dictionary and hash-set lookups are approximately O(1).

questions.prompt: Which statement follows the equality contract?
options: If two objects have the same hash code, they must be equal
Every object must have a unique hash code
questions.explanation: Equal objects must have equal hash codes. The reverse is not guaranteed, because different objects can collide on the same hash code, and if you override `Equals()` you should also override `GetHashCode()` using the same fields.

questions.prompt: The `Geeks` class is declared with `public partial class Geeks` in both `Geeks1.cs` and `Geeks2.cs`. What does the compiler do?
options: It reports a duplicate class error
It merges all the parts into one single class at compile time
It creates two separate classes named `Geeks`
It uses whichever file was compiled last
questions.explanation: A partial class splits one class definition across files; all parts use the `partial` keyword with the same name and namespace, and the compiler merges them into a single class.
